newsitem.title: USA: Georgia GO deal is straightforward, non-callable.
newsitem.headline: Georgia GO deal is straightforward, non-callable.

text.p: Next week's $257 million Georgia GO sale will have a familiar structure -- plain vanilla and all non-callable.

"When they see a state of Georgia bid, they almost know what it is before they read it," said Weyman Smith, director of the state's Finance and Investment Commission. "Other people brag about complexity. I think we would like to brag about simplicity, pretty straightforward issues all the time."
Smith said Georgia GO bonds have priced like strong AAAs even before Standard & Poor's upgraded its rating to AAA, in part because its deals are predictably simple.
"I think that helps us a little bit, at least psychologically," Smith said Wednesday.

Georgia has two GO sales scheduled on Aug 5 by competitive bid -- a $240 million issue with maturities out to 20 years and a $16.44 million issue with maturities out to five years. Like most of the debt Georgia has issued recently, all the bonds are non-callable.
Smith said that was unlikely to change as long as yields on tax-exempt 20-year bonds stay below 6 percent.

"When they start approaching that 6 percent level, I'll start looking at putting the call back on," Smith said. "When you look at the potential for refunding, when long rates are at 5 to 5.15, you've got to go down to 4.15 and probably less to achieve the kind of savings we look for.
"I think the 5 to 10 basis points you may pick up on your non-calls, evaluated against where you've got to go to achieve any savings at all, it's not worth it," Smith said.
